questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Why English people don't bother to learn other languages
How to learn Japanese quickly using apps and films
The life and work of Nelson Mandela in South Africa
People who speak many languages and the benefits of it
questions.why: Neil says people who speak multiple languages benefit from many advantages, as they'll hear.

questions.q: What does Neil say about the English and languages?
options: They are the best language learners in Europe
They are famously slow to learn other languages
They all speak French
They prefer learning Greek
questions.why: Neil says, 'The English are famously slow to learn other languages.'

questions.q: According to Richard Simcott, why do polyglots learn languages?
options: For pleasure or fascination, not because they need to
To get better jobs and earn more money in business
Because they live abroad and need them every day
Because their parents speak many languages at home
questions.why: He says polyglots learn languages they don't need, 'just out of sheer enjoyment, pleasure or fascination'.

questions.q: What is the main idea of Rob's favourite Nelson Mandela quote?
options: It's better to speak only one language well
Learning languages is very difficult
Speaking someone's own language reaches their heart
Everyone should learn English
questions.why: The quote says talking to a man in his own language 'goes to his heart'.

questions.q: What did Eve Fedorenko expect to find in children who speak many languages?
options: Smaller language regions
No difference from other children
Worse speaking skills
Very active language brains
questions.why: Rob says Eve predicted that multilingual children would have hyperactive language brains.

questions.q: What did Eve Fedorenko actually find?
options: Their language regions appeared smaller
Their brains were larger
They forgot their first language
Their language regions were more active
questions.why: She says 'their language regions appear to be smaller, and that was surprising'.

questions.q: Why do the language regions become smaller, according to Eve Fedorenko?
options: Because the children stop practising their languages
Because speaking skills slowly get worse over time
Because the brain becomes more efficient and needs less tissue
Because children are learning far too many languages at once
questions.why: She says as people get better, less brain tissue is needed, so 'you become more efficient'.

questions.q: What is Rob's conclusion at the end of the discussion?
options: Only children should try to learn languages
It is good for the head, heart, mind and soul
Language learning is bad for the brain
It's better to be a polymath than a polyglot
questions.why: Rob says, 'speaking many languages is good for the head, heart, mind and soul!'
